NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule on Friday announced that she would skip the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled for Saturday to discuss the opposition's floor strategy for the special Parliament session , citing her father and party chief Sharad Pawar 's health.With Sharad Pawar hospitalised, the Baramati MP, will remain in Mumbai over the weekend."I will go to Delhi on Monday morning to attend the session," she wrote in her WhatsApp status, PTI reported.Sharad Pawar was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai on Thursday due to dehydration.It remains unclear whether the NCP (SP) will be represented at the meeting and, if so, who will attend on behalf of the party.Sule's announcement came on a day when the NCP (SP) issued a whip directing its Lok Sabha MPs to remain present in the House from November 30, when the special session is scheduled to begin. The move comes amid speculation that the party may support the BJP-led Union government on the proposed delimitation bill.Sule has maintained that her party will examine the draft legislation, if introduced, before taking a final position.NCP (SP) is a constituent of the Congress-led INDIA bloc, which is scheduled to meet at 11.30 am on Saturday at the residence of Congress president and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge.Meanwhile, Congress MP KC Venugopal termed the special session a "big trap" set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for the people of India.He further stated that anyone who believes in the Constitution cannot support what he described as a "divisive" agenda."We are approaching all parties. The DMK has always stood by the Constitution of India. Anyone who believes in the Constitution cannot support such divisive agendas. We will, therefore, reach out to all opposition parties," Venugopal told reporters.The DMK had walked out of the INDIA bloc after the Congress extended support to Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) following the Tamil Nadu assembly elections, paving the way for the party to form the government in the state.The DMK, which was voted out of power, and the Congress had contested the polls as allies. The MK Stalin-led party, too, has reportedly softened its opposition to the delimitation bill, setting two conditions for extending its support.
Article Summary: NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule to skip key INDIA bloc meeting over delimitation bill. Baramati MP, will remain in Mumbai over the weekend. Sharad Pawar was admitted to a hospital in south Mumbai on Thursday due to dehydration.

Article Title: Big win for Mamata: HC sets aside Ritabrata Banerjee's appointment as Bengal LoP

NEW DELHI: The Calcutta high court on Friday quashed the appointment of Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal assembly.A bench of justice Krishna Rao called the decision unsustainable under law and directed the speaker to reconsider and pass a reasoned order.The bench also asked the speaker to reach a fresh decision within 10 days.Following the West Bengal assembly elections earlier this year, assembly speaker Rathindra Bose had recognised Ritabrata Banerjee, leader of the rebel Trinamool Congress faction, as the leader of the opposition and Akhruzzaman as the chief whip.Challenging the speaker's decision, veteran Trinamool Congress MLA Sovandeb Chattopadhyay, a senior leader of the faction led by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, moved the Calcutta high court.Earlier, a division bench of the high court had allowed Ritabrata Banerjee and Akhruzzaman to continue in their respective positions on an interim basis for two months.After the interim period expired on October 18, Chattopadhyay approached the high court again, arguing that neither legislator had any legal right to continue in the posts as the interim arrangement had not been extended.He also alleged that both legislators continued to enjoy state-provided privileges attached to the offices of the leader of the opposition and chief whip despite having no legal authority to hold them.
Article Summary: The Calcutta high court quashed the appointment of Ritabrata Banerjee as the leader of opposition in the West Bengal assembly. A bench of justice Krishna Rao called the decision unsustainable under law. The bench also asked the speaker to reach a fresh decision within 10 days.

Article Title: 'Deepam to be lit tomorrow': Furious SC suspends temple trust, asks CRPF to step in
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp will be lit again on Saturday atop the Deepathoon. It also suspended the Tamil Nadu temple's board of trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to manage the temple, and handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF This order came days after Karthigai Deepam lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, instead of Deepathoon as ordered earlier by the Supreme Court.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said it would take action against anyone attempting to create constitutional chaos.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), told the bench that temple trustees had informed the agency that they had received no instructions from higher officials regarding the entry.Also read: 'Time to deal with iron hand' - SC comes down heavily on Vijay government over Deepam row Here's what SC ordered:The Supreme Court directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop the disputed Deepathoon pillar on Saturday, using the flame lit at the Uchaipillaiyar mandapam. The court had earlier permitted the ritual as a one-time interim measure on November 24, but the lamp was lit only at the customary mandapam and not at Deepathoon.The Supreme Court suspended the board of trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and appointed two retired Madras High Court judges, Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan, as receivers to take over its management.It also handed over security of the temple and Thiruparankundram hill to the CRPF.The bench issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police (DGP), Madurai Collector and other officials over the alleged violation of its November 20 order permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon. Observing that the state executive authorities appeared to have acted on the "diktats of their political bosses", the court directed the chief secretary to appear personally and file an affidavit detailing the emails, phone calls and messages exchanged between officials in connection with the matter.The bench said, "The wilful non-compliance of orders of the Court, especially by the executive authorities, cannot go unnoticed and it has to be dealt with an iron hand." It also observed that the conduct of the officials prima facie indicated administrative chaos in the state. Describing the alleged actions as "a brazen and wilful disobedience" of its order and "a calculated affront to the authority of both constitutional courts", the court warned that attempts to undermine the course of justice would not be tolerated.It further clarified that its orders were binding on the state, its officials and every religious institution, and were not an invitation to negotiate.Expressing "pain and anguish" over the failure to implement its earlier order, the bench said, "The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos."It also warned that it would "set right anybody trying to create constitutional chaos", making it clear that its directions could not be diluted.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Friday ordered that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp will be lit again on Saturday atop the Deepathoon. It also suspended the Tamil Nadu temple's board of trustees, appointed two retired Madras High Court judges as receivers to manage the temple. The bench issued contempt notices to Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary, Director General of Police (DGP), Madurai Collector and other officials.

Article Title: 'One community being favoured': Ex-CJI Gavai writes to President Murmu, cites low OBC, SC and ST representation in judiciary
Article Text:
Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai on Friday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu alleging that judicial appointments increasingly favour candidates from a particular community, raising concerns over inadequate representation of OBCs, SCs, STs, minorities and women in the higher judiciary.Gavai expressed concern over a "growing disregard for diversity, inclusion and merit in judicial appointments and transfers", and sought presidential intervention to ensure equitable representation.In a letter dated November 27, Gavai alleged that a community comprising less than 5% of the country's population had accounted for more than 40% of Supreme Court judges in recent years, without naming the community."I am increasingly becoming concerned that recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he said."A community that is under 5% of the country's population has had over 40% representation in the Supreme Court which has risen manifold in the recent past. While I admit that this is not something new and that is precisely why it is increasingly becoming unforgivable," he added.Clarifying that he was not opposed to candidates from forward communities being considered for judicial appointments, Gavai said his endeavour had always been to ensure a balance between different sections of society.Citing parliamentary data, Gavai said the representation of marginalised communities in the higher judiciary remained inadequate.According to figures presented by Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal in the Rajya Sabha in March 2025, only 22 Scheduled Caste, 16 Scheduled Tribe, 89 OBC and 37 minority candidates were among the 715 High Court judges appointed since 2018.He said roughly three out of every four appointees belonged to the general category, reflecting an imbalance in judicial appointments.Gavai further cited figures for appointments between January 2021 and January 2026, stating that nearly 80% of judicial appointments were from forward communities, while OBC representation remained below 14%."The Other Backward Classes, perhaps 40 to 50% of our people, have received under 14%. Within that pool, one community has been preferred at the Apex Court," he said.He also pointed out that the law ministry had informed a parliamentary committee about the "inequitable representation of backward and minority communities" in the higher judiciary. "Caste is not recorded for Supreme Court appointments, and that silence is itself part of the problem," he added.To underline the historical imbalance, Gavai referred to Professor George Gadbois's study of the Supreme Court's first four decades, which found that a community comprising around one-nineteenth of India's population accounted for more than a third of Supreme Court judgeships between 1950 and 1989.He said the composition of the apex court had remained largely unchanged despite 75 years of the Republic, attributing the persistence of such patterns to familiarity, networks and entrenched perceptions."Seventy-five years into the Republic, the profile of the Court has barely moved. Each of us bears some share of that failure, and I say so plainly. It is because I know how such patterns persist, through familiarity, through networks, and through unexamined ideas of who ‘looks like a Supreme Court judge’, that I can no longer stay silent," he said.Gavai also questioned recent transfers of High Court chief justices, alleging that merit had been overlooked and other considerations had influenced the decisions.He cited the case of a chief justice who was transferred from one High Court to a smaller court and subsequently to one of the country's smallest High Courts before being recommended for transfer to a prominent High Court.Gavai alleged that the latest recommendation came at the expense of another chief justice, whom he described as meritorious and hard-working, who was transferred to a smaller High Court to make way for the former.He said such decisions could demoralise the judges concerned and discourage other hardworking judicial officers, particularly those from marginalised communities.Explaining his involvement in the decisions, Gavai said he was part of the Collegium that recommended the first judge's transfers and headed it when the subsequent transfer was recommended. He also said he had led the Collegium that unanimously recommended the second judge's appointment as chief justice of a prestigious High Court on merit."It therefore raises several unanswered questions as to how a judge transferred multiple times on punitive considerations has for no obvious reasons is now being recommended to be Chief Justice of a much bigger and prominent High Court," he said.Gavai said he had consistently sought to uphold diversity and inclusion during his tenure as a Collegium member and as Chief Justice of India, ensuring representation from forward communities as well as SCs, STs, OBCs, minorities and women in judicial appointments.However, he alleged that recent recommendations had departed from these principles, with candidates from one particular community being favoured over others."When I was a part of the collegium and was Chief Justice of India, I always followed the principles of diversity and inclusion. Adequate representation was ensured to different sections of the society including those belonging to forward section of the society and also to the marginalised section of the society including scheduled casts, tribes, other backward classes, minorities and women, while considering candidates for recommendation for elevation to High court and Supreme Court collegium of which I was a part and later headed it," he said."However, in the recent past disturbing events have unfolded, showing complete disregard to principles of merit and inclusivity. Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalised communities including scheduled casts, tribes, other backward classes, minorities, women and even persons from forward sections of the society who are not from a particular community," he said."I may not be misunderstood as being opposed to any section of the society in so far as the candidate belonging to forward section are duly considered and my endeavour has always been to strike balance between all the sections. However, now there compelling circumstances which support the perception that increasingly recommendations are being made with a focus on appeasing and rewarding a single community," he added.In his concluding appeal, Gavai urged President Murmu to acknowledge the issue and intervene as she deemed appropriate to ensure that all stakeholders were reminded of their constitutional duty to uphold equal representation.
Article Summary: Former Chief Justice of India BR Gavai writes to President Droupadi Murmu. He alleges that judicial appointments increasingly favour candidates from a particular community. He raises concerns over inadequate representation of OBCs, SCs, STs, minorities and women in the higher judiciary.

Article Title: Delimitation row: Kharge calls oppn meet; extends invite to DMK, AAP & BJD
Article Text:
DMK, AAP, BJD invited as Kharge seeks united Opposition stand on delimitation

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge has called a meeting of opposition floor leaders at his residence on Saturday.The meeting aims to formulate a joint strategy ahead of the government's likely move to reintroduce a constitutional amendment bill linked to delimitation, as cited by PTI.The meeting is scheduled for 11.30 am at Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg. Besides INDIA bloc parties, leaders of non-INDIA bloc opposition parties, including the DMK , the AAP and the BJD, have also been invited, sources said, as cited by PTI.The opposition is seeking to coordinate its response to the government's proposed move, with a special sitting of Parliament scheduled to begin on November 30.The Union Cabinet is learnt to have cleared a fresh delimitation-linked women's reservation bill on Friday, raising the possibility of its introduction during the sitting.The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet on December 2. The sittings are scheduled to conclude on December 3, subject to the requirements of government business. Separate directives for reconvening the Houses were issued by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan.The special sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, as Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 but the session was not prorogued.Meanwhile, the Congress has issued a whip to its MPs in both Houses, asking them to remain present during the special sitting. The party has also directed its MPs to reach New Delhi by November 29, a day before the Lok Sabha reconvenes.The Congress on Friday alleged that the proposed sitting was primarily aimed at pushing delimitation and had little to do with women's reservation. Describing it as a desperate move by a "nervous and rattled PM who is under siege", the party said it would oppose the move with firm resolve.The DMK has also reiterated its opposition to any change in the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats among states. Party president M K Stalin on Friday said Tamil Nadu's current 7.18 per cent share of seats in the Lower House should not be reduced under any circumstances.He also said the existing proportion of parliamentary representation among states, determined on the basis of the 1971 Census and subsequently frozen, should remain unchanged for another 25 years.In a statement, Stalin said the DMK remained firm on its demand to protect Tamil Nadu's share of seats and its proportion of representation."No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu’s interests; nor will it depart from its principles," he said.Kharge's meeting is aimed at bringing opposition parties together ahead of the special sitting, with the participation of parties outside the INDIA bloc also expected to be significant in shaping a coordinated response to the proposed legislation.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge calls meeting of opposition floor leaders at his residence. Meeting aims to formulate a joint strategy ahead of government's likely move to reintroduce a constitutional amendment bill linked to delimitation. DMK, AAP, BJD invited as Kharge seeks united Opposition stand on delimitation issue.

Article Title: Cabinet clears 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats across states, ceiling to remain till 2051: Sources
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday approved a proposal to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha by 50% across states, with the revised ceiling to remain in place until 2051, sources told TOI.The decision comes ahead of the special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30, during which the government is expected to take up changes to the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill.The proposed increase in Lok Sabha seats is understood to be part of the government's efforts to address concerns over the impact of delimitation on the representation of states, particularly those in southern India. Earlier reports had indicated that the government was considering a formula to increase seats by 50% across states while retaining their existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.The Cabinet meeting, chaired by PM Modi, was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, with all ministers asked to remain present, sources told ANI.The government is considering amendments to the earlier legislation, which seeks to provide 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.The proposed changes follow the defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha in April.The earlier Bill linked the implementation of women's reservation to delimitation and proposed increasing the strength of the Lok Sabha from the existing 543 seats to a maximum of 850.The special sitting of Parliament will begin with the Lok Sabha reconvening on November 30, while the Rajya Sabha will meet from December 2. The sittings are expected to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.
Article Summary: The Union Cabinet approved a proposal to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha by 50% across states. The decision comes ahead of a special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30. The government is expected to take up changes to the delimitation-linked Women's Reservation Bill.

Article Title: Centre turns up heat on Zakir Naik: States, UTs get sweeping powers under UAPA to act against banned IRF
Article Text:
Fugitive Zakir Naik

NEW DELHI: The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik 's Islamic Research Foundation IRF ), empowering state governments and Union Territory administrations to freeze funds and restrict access to properties linked to the organisation. The move comes days after the home ministry extended a five-year ban on the IRFAccording to a notification issued on Thursday, the Centre has delegated these powers to states and UTs under Section 42 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA)."The Central Government hereby directs that all powers exercisable by it under sections 7 and 8 of the UAPA shall also be exercised by the state governments and the Union territory administrations in relation to the above said unlawful association,” the notification said.The notification also refers to the Centre's November 13 declaration of the IRF as an unlawful association under the UAPA. "In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-sections (1) and (3) of section 3 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 (37 of 1967), the Central Government has declared the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), as an unlawful association vide notification number, S.O. 6182(E), dated the 13th November"Section 7 of the UAPA empowers the government to prohibit the use of funds belonging to an association declared unlawful. It allows authorities to issue a written order barring anyone holding money, securities or credits being used, or intended to be used, for the association from paying, transferring or otherwise dealing with them without the government's written permission.A government-appointed gazetted officer can also be authorised to inspect the person's premises, examine records and investigate financial transactions suspected to be linked to the unlawful association.Section 8, meanwhile, empowers the government to notify any place, including a house, building or part of it, a tent or a vessel, that it believes is being used for the purposes of an unlawful association.Following such a notification, the district magistrate can prepare an inventory of movable property at the premises and prohibit the use of articles suspected to be connected with the association. The magistrate can also restrict entry into the notified premises by people who were not residents there when the notification was issued. Police officers of at least the rank of sub-inspector can search people entering or found at the premises.
Article Summary: The Centre has expanded its crackdown on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation IRF. State governments and Union Territory administrations can freeze funds and restrict access to properties linked to the organisation. The move comes days after the home ministry extended a five-year ban on the IRF

Article Title: 'I have endured a lot': Mamata's brother seeks FIR against nephew Abhishek over 'threats'

NEW DELHI: The younger brother of former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee , Swapan Banerjee on Thursday approached the police seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee , alleging intimidation and obstruction to a blood donation camp, news agency PTI reported.Swapan, popularly known as Babun, alleged that a culture of threats and intimidation had taken root during the TMC's 15-year rule in the state and continued even after the BJP came to power in May this year. He claimed to have witnessed such incidents since 2024."Many things happened during the TMC regime. This has been going on since 2024 and continues even today. I have endured a lot," he told reporters after approaching the Kalighat police station.The immediate trigger for the complaint was allegedly the obstruction of a blood donation camp. However, details of the incident and the specific allegations levelled against the TMC national general secretary were not immediately available.The complaint marks another escalation in the long-standing estrangement between Babun and Mamata Banerjee.The former chief minister had publicly distanced herself from her younger brother at one point, even declaring that she had severed ties with him.The family discord has taken on a political dimension following the BJP's victory in the assembly elections, which ended the TMC's uninterrupted 15-year rule in West Bengal.Since the change of government, Babun has increasingly been seen getting closer to the BJP leadership and has repeatedly praised chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.He recently invited Suvendu Adhikari to inaugurate a community Durga Puja in his neighbourhood and was also seen touching the chief minister's feet as a mark of respect during the event.His repeated public expressions of admiration for Suvendu have fuelled speculation about his political leanings and a possible shift towards the BJP.However, Babun has not made any formal announcement about joining the BJP.
Article Summary: Swapan Banerjee has approached the police seeking registration of an FIR against his nephew and TMC MP Abhishek. Article Title: ‘Today one Deepam, tomorrow temples?’ Vaishnaw slams TVK govt over Thiruparankundram Deepam row
Article Text:
Vaishnaw slams TVK government over Thiruparankundram Deepam row in Tamil Nadu

NEW DELHI: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Thursday launched a sharp attack on the Tamil Nadu government over the Thiruparankundram Karthigai Deepam row, accusing it of hurting the religious sentiments of millions. He also cautioned the state government against attempts to restrict temple traditions and religious practices.Addressing a Constitution Day event organised by the BJP in Chennai, Vaishnaw further targeted the Congress, accusing it of placing family interests above constitutional values.Referring to the dispute over lighting the ceremonial lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar, Vaishnaw questioned the Vijay government's position and warned that restrictions on religious practices could have wider implications."Tamil Nadu is intact. Stopping one deepam, you have stopped, you have hurt, you have destroyed and disturbed the emotions of millions of people. What will happen? Today you have stopped one deepam, tomorrow you will say that nobody can go to a temple? They'll shut down the temples. Is that what they want?" he said, according to news agency PTI.Vaishnaw also said, "True respect for the Constitution means safeguarding religious freedom and taking pride in our culture, Lord Muruga, and our ancient heritage."The remarks came amid continuing tensions over the annual Karthigai Deepam ceremony. Maha Deepam was lit above the Uchi Pillayar temple at Thiruparankundram Hills amid heavy security, but no lamp was lit at the disputed Deepathoon pillar. A team of priests associated with the Subramaniaswamy temple performed the ceremony at the usual location.The dispute escalated after a scuffle broke out between members of Hindu organisations and police. Several people, including BJP leaders and members of Hindu outfits, were detained amid restrictions imposed by authorities over law-and-order concerns.The matter is also before the Supreme Court. On Thursday, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said contempt petitions and other applications concerning the non-lighting of the lamp at Deepathoon would be listed on November 27."Everything will be listed tomorrow," the bench said. The Tamil Nadu government had apologised to the court on Wednesday over the incident, blaming the temple authorities. The apex court had earlier declined to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings.Vaishnaw also criticised the Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and electronic voting machines (EVMs), alleging that the party questioned electoral processes selectively."Congress wants to just blame SIR for their own failures. And they will keep failing like this. Because for them, it is not the Constitution, it is the family," he said.Turning to railway development, the minister claimed that Tamil Nadu had acquired only 1,253 hectares, or 24 per cent, of the approximately 4,800 hectares required for railway projects.He urged the state government to expedite land acquisition, assuring that the Centre would provide the necessary funds. Vaishnaw also highlighted the redevelopment of 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu and discussed proposed high-speed rail connectivity between Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.The Supreme Court's scheduled hearing on Saturday is expected to bring further clarity to the contempt petitions and applications.
Article Summary: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw slams TVK government over Thiruparankundram Deepam row. Accuses Tamil Nadu government of hurting religious sentiments of millions. Warns against attempts to restrict temple traditions and religious practices. Further criticised Congress for placing family interests above constitutional values.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to grant an urgent hearing to a petition challenging the release of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, observing that those who disagree with the film's interpretation of the epic are free to make a film presenting their own perspective.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the urgency of the plea, noting that the film had already been released in theatres and that those interested in watching it had already done so.The petitioner's counsel told the bench that the plea had been registered on November 23 but was yet to be listed for hearing."The movie has already been released. Those who wanted to watch it have already seen it," the CJI said.The counsel argued that "many facts have been distorted" in the film's depiction of the epic. Responding to this, Justice Bagchi said, "They made a movie as they understand, you make a movie as you understand. Don't waste the time of the court."The CJI also remarked, "If you have a counter-view about the epic, you make a movie on the counter-view. Don't waste time of the Court."As the counsel pressed for an early hearing, the bench said the matter would be listed in due course.The petition alleges that the filmmakers distorted mythological facts in their portrayal of the Ramayana.Ramayana: Rise of a Legend, also referred to as Ramayana: Part 1, is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. The film features Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. Its ensemble cast includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh and Vivek Oberoi.The film was released in theatres on November 5, 2026.

Article Title: 'Fake news': CJP's Ranka threatens legal action over claim leaders fled Nagpur rally venue after Look Out Circulars issued

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS, accusing it of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular (LOC), while avoiding media cameras.In its post, IANS wrote: "As soon as they received information about the Look Out Notice, CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates began leaving the spot while avoiding media cameras. They left before Actor Prakash Raj could speak."Responding to the post, Ranka said the agency had published an inaccurate account of the events and warned it to expect a legal notice."Dear IANS, Instead of posting from the IT cell account, you accidentally posted from your official id. You might now wait for a legal notice for spreading fake news, since there are videos of Prakash Sir addressing the audience and all of us comfortably leaving the venue with police around," he wrote on X.The video posted by IANS showed reporters following vehicles carrying CJP leaders as they left the venue. It later showed actor Prakash Raj being escorted by a police official as media personnel gathered around him. However, the footage does not establish the context claimed in the agency's post.The exchange came amid a protest organised by the CJP in Nagpur on Thursday, where Dipke and other party leaders addressed a rally titled 'Save Democracy, Save Constitution' at Samvidhan Chowk on Constitution Day.Addressing the gathering, Dipke accused the BJP-led Centre of undermining the Constitution and alleged that institutions across the country had been hijacked."The government is acting against the Constitution. Not a single institution is left that has not been hijacked," he said.Referring to the LOC issued against him by Mumbai Police, Dipke challenged the authorities to arrest him."There is a lookout notice against me by the Mumbai Police. There is police bandobast here and they are looking for me. Where is Abhijeet Dipke? I am here in Samvidhan Chowk. What will you do? Arrest me. I have been in jail twice. Don't show me the fear of jail," he said.Ranka, meanwhile, said the party was preparing to expand its activities beyond protests in major cities. "We will go to every village, interact with people and give a voice to the youth," he said.Mumbai Police have issued LOCs against Dipke, Ranka and CJP leader Saurav Das in connection with an FIR over an alleged unauthorised protest at Shivaji Park on Gandhi Jayanti. Police said the circulars were issued to prevent the leaders from leaving the country while the investigation was underway.Das was stopped at the airport on November 23 while attempting to travel to the United Kingdom for an event at Oxford University. He has challenged the LOC before the Delhi High Court.
Article Summary: CJP co-convenor Ashutosh Ranka has threatened legal action against news agency IANS. Ranka accused IANS of spreading fake news over a video posted on X. The agency had claimed that CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and his associates left a venue after receiving information about a Look Out Circular.

He questioned the Akhilesh-led party's reluctance to offer the grand old party more seats.Taking a swipe at SP, Saharanpur MP Masood said the Samajwadi Party's tally of 37 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh was made possible in part by Rahul Gandhi's contribution to the INDIA bloc's campaign."It was because of Rahul Gandhi that you (Samajwadi Party)managed to win 37 seats (2024 Lok Sabha Elections). Article Title: 'Money-minded manifesto': Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav's SP ahead of 2027 UP polls

Mayawati slams Akhilesh Yadav

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati on Friday launched a sharp attack on the Samajwadi Party (SP) over its recently released 'Manifesto of the People's Will' for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, dismissing it as "little more than empty rhetoric" and a "money-minded manifesto" rather than a genuine commitment to public welfare.In a post on X, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the SP's manifesto was similar to its 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) initiative and reflected the saying "all show, no substance".Mayawati alleged that the SP had consistently followed a "narrow-minded, casteist and pro-big business" approach that went against the interests, welfare, dignity and security of poor people, Dalits, backward classes, Muslims and other sections of society.She also cited the SP's alleged preference for a wealthy businessperson over supporting the PDA in the recent biennial Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh as an example of its political approach.Questioning whether such policies could address the state's problems, including poverty, unemployment, backwardness and migration, Mayawati said the SP's manifesto was more concerned with financial interests than public welfare.She further alleged that the party would continue to field wealthy candidates and strongmen rather than people committed to public and social interests.Defending her party's record, Mayawati said the principles of "work for every hand" and "the rule of law through the law" belonged to the BSP and had been implemented during all four of its governments in Uttar Pradesh.She also accused the SP of having a record of opposing reservations for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and of contributing to caste-based hostility and riots in the state.In her post, she described the SP's promises and declarations as "electoral deception and trickery", urging voters to remain cautious.Mayawati pitches BSP as authentic Ambedkarite partyWith Assembly elections approaching in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Punjab, Mayawati called for strengthening the BSP, describing it as the only authentic Ambedkarite party capable of translating the ideals of the Constitution into reality.“Given that the general assembly elections—particularly in Uttar Pradesh, as well as in Uttarakhand and Punjab—are fast approaching, it is imperative to effectively translate the noble intent of Babasaheb Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar’s Constitution into reality. This cannot be achieved through the mindset or working culture of narrow-minded, feudal, or casteist parties; rather, it can only be realised through the advancement of the BSP—the sole, authentic Ambedkarite party—which guarantees the welfare of all sections of society and ensures the safety of their lives, property, and religious beliefs, while fostering the upliftment of the 'Bahujan Samaj’," she said.Mayawati said the BSP aimed to establish the rule of law in Uttar Pradesh and promote a governance model centred on public welfare, social well-being and development.“So that an 'iron rule of law' can be established here in UP, along with a governance model rooted in the principle of 'the welfare and happiness of all '—prioritising public interest, social well-being, and development. This would enable all sections of society—currently plagued by poverty, unemployment, backwardness, and the distress of forced migration—to lead a prosperous life filled with peace and happiness,” she added.The BSP, which governed Uttar Pradesh from 2007 to 2012, was reduced to a single seat in the 2022 Assembly elections despite securing more than 13 per cent of the vote share.The party failed to win a single seat in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.SP-Congress seat-sharing talks continueMeanwhile, the SP is preparing to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in alliance with the Congress. The two INDIA bloc partners are continuing negotiations over seat-sharing, with the SP having offered 26 seats to the Congress in the initial round of discussions.The Congress, however, has sought 120 seats and is unwilling to accept a lower number, according to sources.The SP is seeking to return to power after consecutive defeats in the 2017 and 2022 Assembly elections. It won 111 seats in the 2022 polls.
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati slams Samajwadi Party (SP) over its recently released 'Manifesto of the People's Will' for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said the SP's manifesto was similar to its 'PDA' (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) initiative.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday attacked the ruling BJP over the proposed delimitation-linked women's reservation bill, saying it would prove to be the party's “biggest political mistake”.“Delimitation will prove to be the biggest political mistake made by the BJP,” Akhilesh said in a post on X.His remarks came a day after the government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3 to transact “essential” business, amid speculation that it may reintroduce the delimitation-linked women's reservation bill.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.Congress also alleged that the special session had little to do with women's reservation and accused the government of using it to push the delimitation bill.“Yet again, the mischievous PM-HM jodi is lying,” Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said on X.Ramesh pointed out that the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, providing one-third reservation for women, was passed unanimously by Parliament in September 2023.The Congress president had subsequently demanded its immediate implementation, but the law was not notified until 10.40 pm on April 16, 2026, he said.“The Special Session is thus NOT for women's reservation. That is already a law which the PM-HM jodi have put into cold storage for over three years,” Ramesh said.He alleged that the government was convening Parliament to push delimitation and redraw constituencies to benefit the BJP.“And who will be in charge of deciding the geography of constituencies? It will be a thoroughly compromised and brutally exposed CEC, Gyanesh Kumar, who has made a complete mockery of preparation of electoral rolls and destroyed the integrity of the electoral process,” he said.“The executors of Vote Chori on such a gigantic scale are to be given the powers to carry out delimitation and manipulate the nature of constituencies. This is as atrocious as you can get.“This is a desperate move by a nervous and rattled PM who is under siege. It will be countered with firm resolve,” Ramesh added.The Congress has also alleged that the government is hoping to secure a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to pass the Constitution amendment bill.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also opposed the proposed delimitation exercise, alleging that it was a BJP conspiracy to take away people's political power.Sharing a post on X, Raut said, “Today, Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray is no longer with us: Sharad Pawar is unwell and in no position to fight or make decisions, otherwise the anti-national Delimitation Bill would never have dared to be brought before Parliament in such a corrupt manner: Delimitation is a BJP conspiracy to strip the people of this country of their power.”“Anyone who supports it is betraying the people of this country… They will be known as the biggest traitors of the 21st century! Therefore, every patriotic, democratic party should reject Delimitation in Parliament. History always remembers the names of traitors; Explanations for betrayal fade into thin air” he added.Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) is likely to support the delimitation bill, provided it ensures regional balance, party sources told ANI.The Lok Sabha Secretariat said the second part of the eighth session of the 18th Lok Sabha will begin on November 30. The special sitting is expected to conclude on December 3, subject to the exigencies of government business.The sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but not prorogued.Earlier on Thursday, Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Houses to transact essential government business.The Union Cabinet is also scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, sources said.The developments follow Prime Minister Narendra Modi's remarks on Thursday, accusing an opposition party of blocking the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in April.In a signed article published in newspapers, PM Modi, “The journey of our Constitution would be incomplete without recognising the remarkable women who helped shape it. But what happened earlier this year should fill our hearts with shame.”“I assure the 'Nari Shakti' of India that no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them,” he added.The bill was defeated in April after the government failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. It needs 361 votes in the 543-member House, which currently has 540 members due to three vacancies.The NDA has around 320 MPs and would require additional support from opposition parties to cross the threshold.The government's position has strengthened since the bill's defeat in April, with 26 MPs moving out of the opposition camp.Twenty rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.However, the ruling alliance still needs additional votes. The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (SP), with eight, could play a significant role in the evolving political arithmetic.Opposition parties are also expected to raise their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, potentially leading to another stormy session.
Article Summary: The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats. It would pave the way for the implementation of 33% reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections. The government announced a special sitting of Parliament from November 30 to December 3.

Article Title: Big, fat Bihar wedding makes global headlines
Article Text:
Global news outlet carried the headline, 'Politician hosts 4,00,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state', adding six helipads had been built for the purpose and 500 cooks had prepared a feast.

With 150 dishes on menu, finding a plate became the real challenge

The wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh ’s daughter, Shivangi, over five days in his ancestral village of Nadwan in Patna district has created such a buzz that it has grabbed the attention of global media.The sheer scale of the ostentatious celebrations and feudal display of wealth and power, in the backdrop of the many criminal cases the MLA faces, became an irresistible story for the world media. That it’s happening in Bihar, the country’s poorest state, is an irony that echoes through the coverage.BBC observed that “the extravagant wedding in Bihar, a state where one in every three citizens is counted as multidimensionally poor, has been dubbed ‘a royal wedding’ and become a huge talking point.” It added that a political rival of the MLA has called for a probe into the source of money spent.The Guardian carried the headline, “Politician hosts 4,00,000 guests at daughter’s wedding in India’s poorest state”, adding six helipads had been built for the purpose and 500 cooks had prepared a feast. Daily Mail called it a “big fat Indian wedding” in the “country’s poorest state”. It added the “scale was staggering even by standards of India’s famed extravagant weddings that last for days.”Held on Nov 25, Mokama MLA Anant Singh’s younger daughter Shivangi’s wedding to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit turned into an extraordinary spectacle with preparations for lakhs of guests, a horse race, a massive feast, luxury cars and five helipads.Anant had made it clear that invitations were not restricted to Bihar, extending them across India and even Pakistan. “Everyone who has shown us love will come. The public is like God to us; whoever comes from wherever will be a gift to me. Koi cinema thodi hai jo ticket lagega.”More than 10 bighas (6.2 acres) were developed into a grand venue featuring a Jaipur-inspired pavilion, a massive stage and imported flowers. The groom’s procession comprised 151 vehicles, while separate arrangements were made for guests and dignitaries.But food arrangements, despite 500 cooks and over 300 cooking stations, struggled to cope with the turnout.Videos showed disposable plates being thrown into the crowd with guests scrambling to catch them. Some used cardboard, newspapers, and even drinking glasses to carry food. Others were seen picking paneer directly from vessels, while a video purportedly showed a man falling into a “sabzi” vessel.Sticks were used to control the crowd. One guest described getting food there like winning a war, regretting that rasgullas had disappeared before he could get to them. With more than 150 dishes on the menu, finding a plate became the real challenge.The race featuring over 20 horses from Bihar, UP, Rajasthan and Delhi offered a Thar to the winner, a motorcycle to the runner-up, and a scooter to the second runner-up. Spectators climbed trees and high-tension electricity towers to watch, forcing the organisers to halt the competition and postpone the finale.The groom’s luxury car got stuck in traffic for hours, prompting the bride’s brothers to pull him out. Anant’s vintage open Jeep was used to bring him to the wedding stage.Traffic stretched for 8-10 km, leaving commuters and VIPs stranded. Bihar assembly speaker Prem Kumar’s convoy remained stuck for hours, while some walked through fields to reach the venue.Anant’s own arrival was equally dramatic. He stood up to look out of his SUV’s sunroof, waving an orange ‘gamcha’ amid cheering supporters. His entry looked less like a father arriving at his daughter’s wedding and more like a political roadshow.Meanwhile, allegations of animal cruelty during the celebrations have prompted an animal welfare activist to seek separate investigations into the alleged use of an iron “ankush” on a captive elephant and the horse-racing event.Chief scout Naresh Kadyan, master trainer of the Animal Welfare Board of India, has submitted a legal notice-cum-statutory representation to the Bihar government over alleged coercive handling of an elephant. He has also approached the Bihar assembly’s committee on petitions, seeking an independent inquiry into the horse-racing event held on Nov 25.With the bride’s ‘bidaai’ taking place Thursday, the MLA can breathe easy before he heads for jail on Dec 4 in a murder case. His bail has been cancelled by the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: The wedding of Mokama MLA Anant Singh ’s daughter, Shivangi, over five days in his ancestral village of Nadwan in Patna district has grabbed the attention of global media. The sheer scale of the ostentatious celebrations and feudal display of wealth and power, in the backdrop of the many criminal cases the MLA faces, became an irresistible story for the world media.

Article Title: Special Parliament session from November 30; women’s quota on agenda
Article Text:
Smarting under the govt’s first defeat on the floor of Parliament, BJP has since made determined moves to shore up its numbers, helped considerably by fractures in the opposition camp.

Shah’s assurance may be added to delimitation bill, Cabinet nod today

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ending suspense, government Thursday moved to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30 during which it is expected to bring back the delimitation bills to implement the women’s quota law from 2029, which would increase Lok Sabha’s maximum strength to 850 from 550, reflecting confidence in NDA that it will muster a two-thirds majority this time to secure the bill’s passage.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that government has requested Speaker Om Birla to reconvene Lok Sabha on November 30 and Rajya Sabha Chairman C P Radhakrishnan to call a sitting of the House on Dec 2 to transact “essential government business”.“Subject to exigencies of business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on Dec 3, 2026,” he said, suggesting government is hopeful of concluding its agenda in four days.This is the second attempt by government to secure passage of its ambitious legislative agenda. If passed, it will mark the biggest realignment of Lok Sabha constituencies since Independence. A united opposition had thwarted the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in a similarly convened session, of three days, from April 16.The move comes amid strong indications that government is confident of its numbers in the second trial of strength that the opposition is determined to force.In any case, it will be loath to risk another embarrassment; that too one during the build-up to assembly elections in UP and other states.Passage of the bill, which will ensure reservation of one-third seats in Lok Sabha and pave the way for a similar quota in assemblies, will give BJP a major campaign point in the upcoming polls to showcase its pro-women credentials.In an article on Thursday, PM Narendra Modi said the scuttling of the bill earlier this year “should fill our hearts with shame”, adding that a legislation aimed at giving adequate representation to women was prevented from being passed by one opposition party, in what was an attack at Congress.He assured women that “no force can prevent us from ensuring that justice is done to them.”Last time, among 528 MPs present in Lok Sabha, the bill had received support from 298 members while 230 opposed it, falling way short of the 352 needed for its passage.Smarting under the government’s first defeat on the floor of Parliament, BJP has since made determined moves to shore up its numbers, helped considerably by fractures in the opposition camp.The switchover of 20 of 29 Trinamool Congress Lok Sabha MPs to NDA has boosted its numbers. Going by the buzz within government, it is also counting on support of 22 DMK MPs and eight of NCP-SP, who had voted against the bill last time along with TMC’s entire lot.Lok Sabha’s current strength is 540, with NDA’s tally at 321. The support of DMK and NCP-SP will take it to 351. The expected support from four YSR Congress MPs will take it closer to the 360-mark required in case all 540 MPs vote, which is unlikely as a few abstentions are expected to NDA’s advantage.Government has maintained secrecy about its potential new backers. DMK and NCP-SP have not announced support but have suggested that they can back the bill if states are not discriminated against — a threshold that government can easily meet by writing into the bill, which is already in Parliament, a clause providing for 50 per cent increase in seats across the board.Union minister Amit Shah had assured Lok Sabha in April that no state would suffer erosion in its relative strength in the lower House as the number of seats in each state would rise by around 50 per cent. The strength of state assemblies will be next to go up if the bill is passed. Shah’s assurance may be pencilled into the bill, which the Union cabinet headed by PM Narendra Modi is likely to clear Friday.A DMK MP told TOI that party chief MK Stalin will finalise their stand after looking at the bill, reiterating that southern states should not suffer. DMK has anyway drifted away from the opposition after Congress dumped it to align with CM Vijay-led TVK in Tamil Nadu.NCP MP Supriya Sule said “let the bill be out first”, suggesting her openness to the proposal. She said the bill may be good and needed to be studied first, and that opposition and government had in the past supported decisions which were in national interest.The hard part for the government is in the Lok Sabha, as its numbers are more favourably aligned in the Rajya Sabha.
Article Summary: Government moves to convene a short session of Parliament from November 30. It is expected to bring back the delimitation bills to implement the women’s quota law from 2029. A united opposition had thwarted the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill in a similarly convened session, of three days, from April 16.

Article Title: Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das
Article Text:
Senior counsel Akhil Sibal, representing Das, told Justice Amit Mahajan that his client had never been told of a lookout circular against him. He asked for a copy of the document along with an explanation of its “purpose”.

Can’t give LOC copy as Das yet to respond to Nov 23 notice: Government

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Centre informed Delhi high court on Thursday that a lookout circular had been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das at the request of Mumbai police early on Nov 23, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport barred him from flying to London. Besides Das, lookout circulars have been issued against CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka over CJP’s protest at Dadar on October 2.Centre’s counsel said Das was free to challenge the circular in the appropriate court, reiterating that the CJP functionary also faces scrutiny for “multiple discrepancies” in his passport that could affect his citizenship.Das’s lawyers had filed a petition seeking clarity on why he was issued a notice about alleged discrepancies in his passport on the day he was to fly to UK.“The LOC is clearly an afterthought,” Das said in a statement later, asking why declared fugitives such as Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi had been allowed to leave the country while activists like him were being stopped.Senior counsel Akhil Sibal, representing Das, told Justice Amit Mahajan that his client had never been told of a lookout circular against him. He asked for a copy of the document along with an explanation of its “purpose”.The counsel said enforcement agencies were awaiting the outcome of an inquiry that started in Puducherry to verify Das’s place of birth, address and parentage, pointing out that the passport column meant to have details of his father had been left blank.He said that, assuming passport authorities find Das’s explanation inadequate, he could be “left stranded in no-man’s land”.Additional solicitor general Chetan Sharma and standing counsel Ashish Dixit said a copy of the lookout circular could not be immediately given to Das because he was yet to respond to the show-cause notice issued on Nov 23.That notice, Sharma said, states that inputs were received indicating Das’s place of birth was incorrect and that his passport had been obtained by suppressing facts. “It requires clarification and supporting documents, failing which the passport may be suspended or impounded,” he said.The ASG also told the court that Madras HC issued notice on a plea seeking an inquiry into Das’s antecedents on Oct 30.Sibal countered that a pending show-cause notice over discrepancies could not translate into a travel ban. “There is no revocation, suspension, impounding of the passport. The show-cause notice doesn’t mean necessarily there will be harsh consequences… he will respond to the notice in due course,” he said, arguing that travel was a fundamental right.
Article Summary: Centre informed Delhi high court on Thursday that a lookout circular had been issued against CJP co-convener Saurav Das. The circular was issued at the request of Mumbai police early on Nov 23, hours before immigration officials at Delhi airport barred him from flying to London. Das’s lawyers had filed a petition seeking clarity on why he was issued a notice about alleged discrepancies in his passport.

NEW DELHI: Quoting former US President Theodore Roosevelt to say justice consisted not in being neutral between right and wrong, but in finding out the right and upholding it, the Supreme Court Thursday quashed Bihar’s decision to allow the premature release of former MP and strongman Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case of district magistrate G Krishnaiah.The state government had amended prison rules to pave the way for Mohan’s release by removing the provision that disqualifies a person from remission if he is convicted of a public servant’s murder. A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu quashed the amendment, saying it was indefensible and no rationale was given for changing the law. It directed Mohan to surrender within a month.“The notification dated April 10, 2023, is declared unconstitutional, invalid and inoperative, and is hereby set aside. The order dated April 24, 2023, granting premature release to (Mohan), is hereby quashed,” the bench said.The court said the state government could initiate a fresh procedure to amend the remission policy. “It is clarified that any future process to revise or amend Rule 481 shall not be initiated prior to (Mohan) surrendering within a month or being taken into custody, as the case may be,” it said.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court Thursday quashed Bihar’s decision to allow the premature release of former MP and strongman Anand Mohan in the 1994 lynching case of district magistrate G Krishnaiah. Article Title: Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days
Article Text:
Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati informed a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalay Bagchi and V Mohana that in the 22 cases, HDFC, ICICI, Samman and PNB have granted conditional sanction for prosecution

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has read out the riot act and asked HDFC Bank ICICI Bank , Sammaan Capital and PNB Home Finance to grant unconditional sanction within a week to prosecute their bank officials, who are charged by CBI for colluding with builders in the alleged duping of homebuyers under the subvention schemes, or remain present in court to explain the lapse.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati said CBI, as directed by the SC, had inquired into 55 cases pan-India and has filed chargesheets in 22 cases, closed 3 cases and expects to complete the probe into the rest in three months.Bhati informed a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalay Bagchi and V Mohana that in the 22 cases, HDFC, ICICI, Samman and PNB have granted conditional sanction for prosecution, which is creating doubts in the minds of trial courts in taking cognisance of the chargesheet and proceeding with framing of charges.When senior advocate Sanjiv Sen, appearing for HDFC, said that sanction has been granted but there are certain rulings of the constitutional courts that flag the issue of whether private bank officials are public servants requiring sanction for prosecution. Moreover, the officials charged have been exonerated of wrongdoing in the internal inquiry, Sen said.The CJI-led bench said what else but exoneration of officials is expected in internal inquiries by banks, which had hobnobbed with rogue builders and cheated the homebuyers by releasing large sums of loan instalments to the builders even when there was hardly any progress in the construction of housing projects.When Sen protested against grant of sanction citing a judgment, the bench differentiated and said this is a court-monitored investigation, and hence SC can direct the banks to grant unconditional sanction for prosecution of delinquent officials.The bench said, “We direct all banks to issue unconditional sanction for prosecution within a week, failing which their CMDs shall remain present in court to explain why action should not be taken against them.”The bench said once the sanction is granted, the trial courts will expeditiously take cognisance of CBI chargesheets and begin trial as per law. It also directed CBI to conclude investigations into the remaining cases expeditiously and not later than two months.On Aug 6, SC said that in court-monitored investigations, sanction for prosecution should be granted promptly and directed the banks to give necessary permissions within two weeks for prosecution of the accused bank officials. “Failure to accord sanction within two weeks would require banks to submit explanations to the court,” it had said and asked the CBI to share documents on the money trail with the ED to kick off an inquiry under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

Article Title: ‘105 days of Operation Lotus’: Opposition targets Centre over special Parliament sitting amid delimitation bill buzz
Article Text:
File photo

Congress alleges attempt to secure numbers for Constitution amendment

CPI(M) MP alleges political manoeuvring to push delimitation

What is behind the special sitting?

NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Thursday criticised the Centre's decision to convene a special sitting of Parliament from November 30, alleging that the move was aimed at securing the numbers to pass the delimitation-linked Constitution amendment Bill that was defeated in April.Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh accused the Narendra Modi government of attempting to manufacture a two-thirds majority after what he described as "105 days of Operation Lotus", while Congress MP Manish Tewari said the proposed sitting mocked Parliament and should not replace the regular Winter Session.Communist Party of India (Marxist) MP John Brittas also alleged that the government was using political manoeuvring to secure support for delimitation under the cover of the Women's Reservation Bill.The reactions came after Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30 and the Upper House on December 2 to transact essential government business. The sittings may conclude on December 3, depending on the business, he said.In a post on X, Ramesh linked the announcement to the government's earlier attempt to pass the delimitation-linked legislation, which failed to secure the required majority in April."On the evening of Ambedkar Jayanti on April 14, 2026, the Modi Govt had made the Delimitation Bills public that met their well-deserved fate on the night of April 17, 2026."Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi Govt announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill. Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution?"The fight is on," he wrote.Tewari, the Congress MP from Chandigarh, questioned the decision to convene a special sitting instead of a regular Winter Session."This request mocks the institution of Parliament. It is time for the Winter Session to convene. A special session is a mechanism for convening sitting during the inter-session period. It can and should not become a substitute for a regular Winter Session," he said in a post tagging Rijiju."Why not just convene a regular Winter Session when the government can, if it chooses, 'regurgitate' defeated legislation," he added.The proposed sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 but has not been formally prorogued.Brittas alleged that the government was attempting to secure a parliamentary majority through political mergers and defections to push through the delimitation exercise."Modi Govt's so-called amalgamations, takeovers, mergers and buyouts appear to have one sinister objective: manufacture a majority to push through delimitation under the guise of the Women's Reservation Bill. The real 'expenditure' for the session will be humongous!!" he wrote on X.He also cautioned against using women's empowerment as a cover for changes to the country's electoral framework."A majority manufactured through political manipulation is not a mandate. It is a mockery of democracy. If this is how India's electoral future is being reshaped, the special session of Parliament on November 30 could mark the saddest chapter in the history of Indian democracy. Women's empowerment must never become a smokescreen for electoral engineering," Brittas added.Congress MP Karti P Chidambaram, meanwhile, appeared to suggest that the BJP may have secured the support of the DMK and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) for the proposed legislation."Guess the BJP government has got its ducks in a row!" he wrote on X, tagging the official accounts of the BJP, DMK and NCP-SP.However, NCP-SP MP Shashikant Shinde said his party would decide its position only after examining the proposed legislation."There is a lot of discussion today about what delimitation might look like, but no bill or proposal has been presented yet. Once the proposal is introduced in the session, our party's MPs will study it and discuss it in Parliament," he said.Shinde added that party leaders Supriya Sule and Amol Kolhe would decide the party's position and course of action after the details were made available.Sule had also recently said it would be premature to oppose the delimitation Bill before its contents were known. "Let the bill come. Perhaps there could be something good in the Delimitation Bill," she told news agency PTI.The announcement has renewed speculation that the government may reintroduce the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation and facilitate the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in legislatures.The Bill, introduced in April along with the Delimitation Bill, 2026 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, failed to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha on April 17.A constitutional amendment requires the support of at least 361 members in the present 543-member House. With three vacancies, the Lok Sabha currently has 540 members. The ruling NDA has around 320 MPs and would need additional support to cross the threshold.The political arithmetic has changed since the Bill's defeat. According to the PTI background report, 20 rebel Trinamool Congress MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA, while six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.The DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP-SP, with eight, could also play a role in the numbers required.The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet on Friday and is likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's reservation legislation, according to sources.A Congress Parliamentary Strategy Group meeting is also scheduled for Friday to discuss the party's approach to the parliamentary sitting.The opposition INDIA bloc has demanded that the 33 per cent women's reservation be implemented in the existing 543-member Lok Sabha, without linking it to delimitation.The government, meanwhile, has maintained that delimitation is necessary to reflect updated population data and facilitate the implementation of the quota.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday reiterated his commitment to women's representation, saying no force could prevent the government from ensuring justice for women. He also blamed an opposition party for the defeat of the Constitution amendment Bill in April.
Article Summary: Congress alleges attempt to secure numbers for Constitution amendment.CPI(M) MP alleges political manoeuvring to push delimitation. Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the Lower House on November 30.

Article Title: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
Article Text:

Delhi HC: No proof of ‘ anti-government activism ’ charge against NGO

NEW DELHI: Taking a dim view of the home ministry’s reluctance to share even with the court the inputs that led it to cancel the FCRA licence of an NGO engaged in legal aid, Delhi high court on Thursday set aside the decision. HC said the move to cancel the licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC) based solely on the allegation that it has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was without any material.HC said no material was furnished by government to show that SLIC’s activities would likely prejudicially affect the sovereignty, integrity or security of India or the public interest.While government contends that the violations on the appellant’s NGO’s part were brought to its notice through ‘security inputs’, which cannot be divulged since they are ‘secret’; this court is of the view that such inputs cannot be kept secret to the point that no material is brought even to the notice of this court, though the appellant has faced the drastic action of having its FCRA registration cancelled, arising from such inputs,” Justice AJ Bhambhani of Delhi HC said.“The respondent’s (Centre) allegation that the appellant has indulged in ‘aggressive anti-government political activism’ is also not based on any material. No documents or other material has been placed on record by the respondent to support that allegation,” HC added in its judgement.It said unless something sinister comes through from material available against it, an organisation that is engaged in assisting aggrieved persons in raising their grievances before courts and statutory commissions, acting through the available constitutional machinery, cannot be characterised as engaging in “political activity” or in activities impinging on political and law-and-order domains.“In the impugned cancellation order, the respondent has also alleged that the appellant’s activities amount to an attempt to portray a ‘wrong image of public institutions of India in the eyes of international community’. This court would observe that this allegation strains credulity; and this court is dismayed by the respondent’s attempt to baselessly portray the appellant organisation in such light,” it said.HC’s verdict came on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the Oct 2022 order of the home ministry cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. The NGO also challenged the freezing of its designated foreign contribution account and its utilisation accounts maintained with several banks across the country.
Article Summary: HC’s verdict came on a plea by the NGO seeking to set aside the Oct 2022 order of the home ministry cancelling its Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act registration certificate. Delhi high court said the move to cancel the licence of NGO Socio Legal Information Centre (SLIC) based solely on the allegation that it has indulged in “aggressive anti-government political activism” was without any material.

Article Title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
Article Text:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday called out the “double standard” of multinational companies in producing foodstuff for Indian consumers inferior in quality to what they did in Western countries, saying it was “deeply troubling”.While directing FSSAI to enforce front-of-pack nutrition labelling (FoPNL) to make consumers aware of the contents of packaged food, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran deliberated on the dual yardsticks MNCs follow.“Concerns have been raised that certain multinational FBOs operating in India adopt practices towards Indian consumers that differ from those they follow elsewhere, including in the composition of their products and in the information provided on their labels. Such companies comply with, and in some instances voluntarily adopt, FoPNL requirements in other jurisdictions, yet resist similar measures here. If true, such double standards are deeply troubling,” the bench said.Saying a consumer in India was entitled to “no less protection and no less information” than one in the US or UK, SC said, “We would urge such multinational FBOs to adopt uniform standards across jurisdictions, and to extend to Indian consumers the same regard and respect for their health that they extend to consumers elsewhere.”It also directed FSSAI to ensure FBOs do not conceal or alter the composition of their products, or add additives, artificial preservatives, emulsifiers, etc, to soften the effect of FoPNL. “The introduction of a warning label must not become an occasion for reformulation that is hidden from the consumer, or that places the consumer at comparable or greater risk,” SC said.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran deliberated on the dual yardsticks MNCs follow. “Concerns have been raised that certain multinational FBOs operating in India adopt practices towards Indian consumers that differ from those they follow elsewhere,” they said.

Article Title: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions.

NEW DELHI: In an important insertion into the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, the Supreme Court on Friday said the bench of the adjudicating authority (AA), tasked with deciding the confirmation of ED’s orders for provisional attachment of assets by terming them proceeds of crime, must have a judicial member.Deciding a host of petitions questioning the competence of administrative members forming single-member benches to decide questions of law and conflicting judgements from various HCs, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions.“The presence of a judicial member on the bench undertaking the same ensures legal objectivity in the determination recorded by the AA. The lifetime of experience of the administrative and financial members in the AA would undoubtedly render them to be exceptional experts in their fields, but impartial and legally sound adjudication necessitates judicial temperament and training,” the bench said.It added, however, that the judgment would operate prospectively and not provide grounds for the reopening of past decisions.
Article Summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that to confirm confiscation of assets termed as ‘proceeds of crime’ under Section 8 of PMLA, the AA is required to analyse legal provisions. The presence of a judicial member on the bench ensures legal objectivity in the determination recorded by the AA.
