NEW DELHI: Congress MP Imran Masood refused to temper his criticism of the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, despite party chief Mallikarjun Kharge 's call for unity. Claiming he was being "cornered from all sides" and made a "villain", Masood questioned, "Does BJP 's defeat rest only on my shoulders?", taking another swipe at the INDIA bloc ally over its approach to the proposed alliance.Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, Masood said Kharge had acknowledged his efforts and appreciated his work, while maintaining that he would continue to raise concerns in the Congress's interest."Kharge ji has acknowledged my efforts; he is appreciating my work. I am prepared to sacrifice my very life for the progress of my party. I am being cornered from all sides, as if I am a villain."Masood added, "I am making demands for my party; I am fighting for my party. I will always speak in the interest of my party. An alliance is being formed; does the entire responsibility of ousting the BJP rest solely on my shoulders? Does it not rest on yours (SP) as well?"The party MP also questioned the SP's approach to allocating constituencies, arguing that the Congress should not be offered seats where it had little chance of winning.“Give us seats; we can contest and win. We need both quality and quantity... You take the Chief Minister’s post. There is no dispute here regarding the Chief Minister. But why are you trying to undermine your ally? Why do you want to belittle your ally? You started launching direct attacks against me; why? I hadn’t said a single word against you," he said.He further argued that the Congress's contribution to the alliance should not be measured only by its past electoral performance."The Congress is zero. You keep reminding us of our standing, but if you think so little of our standing, why do you even need us? You have the formula for winnability; you have everything, so why do you need us at all?... We are zero—but wherever we align, we multiply the impact tenfold. It was because of Rahul Gandhi that you (SP) managed to win 37 seats (2024 Lok Sabha Elections). We aren’t saying you didn’t contribute; we are saying that we, too, secured victories. We showed a big heart, but must it always be us who shows a big heart, every single time? Can’t you show a bit more generosity?" he told ANI.The disagreement intensified after the SP reportedly offered 26 seats as a starting point and announced five candidates while negotiations were underway. Masood had objected to the move, saying: "We are not beggars... Somewhere, this is very hurtful: that you will dictate terms like this."On Thursday, Kharge, addressing the Congress's Samvidhan Raksha Sammelan in Lucknow, said Masood spoke with enthusiasm but stressed the need for collective effort. "But more than statements, we have to work on the ground," he said.The Congress is reportedly seeking around 130 seats, while the SP's initial offer was 26.
Article Summary: Congress MP Imran Masood refuses to temper his criticism of the Samajwadi Party over seat-sharing for the poll-bound Uttar Pradesh. Claiming he was being "cornered from all sides" and made a "villain", Masood questioned, "Does BJP's defeat rest only on my shoulders?", taking another swipe at the INDIA bloc ally.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday rejected a plea seeking the removal of videos showing Italian politician Giacomo Filibeck raising the slogan 'Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod' at a Congress-organised event in Hyderabad.The plea had also asked for an independent SIT probe into the participation of foreign delegates and the permissions granted to them for attending the event.During an earlier mentioning before Chief Justic Surya Kant, the petitioner's counsel alleged the secretary-general of the Party of European Socialists (PES), had interfered in India's domestic politics by criticising the government and expressing support for the Opposition.The plea came after Filibeck's remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026, held in Hyderabad on November 13 and 14. He had expressed support for Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and the Congress, saying democracy was "under attack" in India and calling for international support to defend it.His use of the slogan, popularised by Rahul Gandhi, drew criticism from the BJP , which accused the Congress of allowing foreign political representatives to comment on India's internal affairs.Filibeck also said the PES, Congress and other political movements across the world were part of a progressive alliance committed to social justice, climate justice, human rights and democracy."True democracy. Not the corrupted one, not the rigged one, not the fake one," he said.The Party of European Socialists (PES) is a transnational European political party that brings together socialist, social democratic, and labour parties across Europe.Around 1,000 delegates, policymakers and thinkers from 70 countries, were present at The Bharat Summit 2026, which held discussions over geopolitics, democracy, climate change, artificial intelligence and progressive politics.

""Implement one-third reservation for women and reservation within reservation for women belonging to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes from the 2029 Lok Sabha elections," Ramesh said in a post on X.Congress deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi also questioned the government's decision to convene a short special sitting without provisions for Question Hour, Zero Hour or private members' bills."No question hour, No zero hour, No Private Members bill in Parliament. Yesterday when the entire country paid homage to Dr. BabaSaheb Bhim Rao Ambedkar, the Lok Sabha issued a bulletin for a short 4 day Parliament session without any question hour, zero hour or private member bill."Does the Parliament belong to Modi-Shah?" he asked on X.The Congress's remarks came a day after Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju announced that the government had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Rajya Sabha Chairman to reconvene the two Houses on November 30 and December 2, respectively."Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026," Rijiju said in a post on X.The sitting will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, as Parliament was adjourned sine die on August 13 and has not been prorogued.Although the government has not officially confirmed the legislative business to be taken up, speculation has centred on the proposed Delimitation Bill and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.The Congress has alleged that the government is seeking to revive its delimitation-linked constitutional amendment proposal to secure the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha.On Thursday, Ramesh said the government had made the delimitation Bills public on April 14, Ambedkar Jayanti, but they were defeated in Parliament on April 17."Now on Constitution Day, after 105 days of Operation Lotus, the Modi government announces a special session, hoping that it will get its super-tainted two-thirds majority to pass a Constitution amendment bill," he said.Questioning the timing of the special sitting, Ramesh asked whether there could be a greater insult to and assault on the Constitution, adding, "The fight is on."

NEW DELHI: A special sitting of Parliament will begin on November 30, with the government expected to consider reviving its push for a constitutional amendment linking women’s reservation to delimitation. The move could set the stage for a fresh political confrontation with the Opposition.The Lok Sabha will reconvene on November 30 and the Rajya Sabha on December 2, with the sittings scheduled to conclude on December 3, subject to government business.The government has not officially confirmed which Bills will be taken up. However, speculation has gathered pace over the proposed Delimitation Bill and the implementation of 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures ahead of the 2029 general elections.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses to transact “essential government business”.“Subject to exigencies of the business, the sitting of both Houses may conclude on December 3, 2026,” Rijiju said in a post on X.The special sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13 and subsequently prorogued.The proposed legislation seeks to increase the Lok Sabha's strength from 543 to a maximum of 850 seats through delimitation, paving the way for 33 per cent reservation for women in legislative bodies.The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha during the special sitting on April 16-17. It received 298 votes in favour and 230 against, with 11 members abstaining. At the time, the House had 528 members and the Bill needed 352 votes to pass.The draft had not provided for a proportional 50 per cent increase in seats across states, a key concern for regional parties, particularly those from southern India. The government has since explored a formula to increase seats by 50 per cent in every state while retaining the existing inter-state share based on the 1971 Census.The opposition parties are also expected to carry their protests against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation into Parliament.The BJP leaders are banking on support from the DMK, NCP-SP and breakaway factions of the Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena for the delimitation bill. The DMK has 22 Lok Sabha MPs and the NCP (SP) has eight. Both parties have indicated they could consider backing the proposal if their states' share of seats is protected.NCP-SCP MP Supriya Sule on Wednesday said the proposed Delimitation Bill should first be introduced and its full text made available for scrutiny. “Let the bill be introduced first; let us have the full bill in our hands. Once we have it, we can discuss it—and perhaps it will turn out to be a good one,” she told reporters.YSRCP is also expected to support the Delimitation Bill, according to sources quoted by news agency ANI. Meanwhile, Congress and NCP (SP) are stepping up coordination ahead of the sitting, with the parties summoning their MPs to discuss the proposed legislation and the Opposition's strategy.Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said the government was hoping to secure its “super-tainted” two-thirds majority. “A fight is on,” he said.The Union Cabinet is scheduled to meet at Sewa Teerth in New Delhi at 1 pm on Friday.The meeting comes as the BJP holds a two-day gathering of its national office-bearers and state in-charges at the PUSA campus on November 27 and 28. Discussions are expected to cover organisational strategy, upcoming Assembly elections and coordination between the Centre, states and the party organisation.The Cabinet meet is also likely to discuss the delimitation-linked women's quota, ANI wrote, quoting sources.
Article Summary: Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said the government had requested Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and Rajya Sabha chairman C P Radhakrishnan to reconvene the Houses. The special sittings will be an extension of the Monsoon Session, which was adjourned sine die on August 13.

Article Title: India wins the Visitors’ Lion at the 61st Venice Art Biennale as NMACC anchors a historic return
Article Text:
“The National Pavilion of India at La Biennale di Venezia, features some of our most compelling artistic voices. The richness and plurality of their work reflect the complexities and creative ambition of contemporary India, while celebrating the timeless traditions of our country. This project underscores our vision for

art and culture

to foster a global dialogue that transcends boundaries, bringing the best of India and the world together.”

Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home

In Minor Keys

India has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, capping a triumphant return after a seven-year hiatus. Decided by public vote, the honour recognises a pavilion that drew roughly 4.5 lakh visitors at the Arsenale.At the heart of this milestone sits the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC), whose institutional muscle, championed by Founder and Chairperson Nita Ambani and Director Isha Ambani, placed contemporary Indian art squarely at the centre of global dialogue.For Isha Ambani, the victory marks a defining chapter in NMACC’s founding ambition.Speaking on the pavilion’s significance, she said:That vision was evident from opening week in May, when Isha Ambani co-hosted a landmark dinner at Venice’s Scuola Grande della Misericordia alongside curator Dr. Amin Jaffer, with Nita Ambani in attendance. Gathering international museum directors, curators, and collectors, the evening also highlighted how NMACC’s Mumbai programming feeds India’s global footprint, with exhibiting artists Asim Waqif and Ranjani Shettar having previously shown at Art House, NMACC.Presented by the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in collaboration with the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre and Serendipity Arts Foundation, and curated by Dr. Amin Jaffer, the National Pavilion of India showcased the exceptional works of Alwar Balasubramaniam, Ranjani Shettar, Sumakshi Singh, Skarma Sonam Tashi and Asim Waqif. Titled, the exhibition responded to the Biennale’s theme,, examining belonging through Tamil Nadu clay, embroidered thread, botanical sculptures, Ladakhi papier-mâché, and bamboo.Complemented by Serendipity Arts’ city-wide performance programme, this public-voted triumph sets a formidable benchmark ahead of the Ministry of Culture’s upcoming The India Biennale, opening in New Delhi on 4 December 2026 across heritage sites including Purana Qila and the Red Fort.
Article Summary: India has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia. Decided by public vote, the honour recognises a pavilion that drew roughly 4.5 lakh visitors.

Article Title: MNS leader threatens protest over Diljit Dosanjh concert, seeks ban on large events
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), led by Raj Thackeray, has urged Mumbai Police to impose an immediate ban on live music concerts and large-scale entertainment events at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and the NSCI Dome, alleging recurring incidents of drug consumption, traffic congestion and civic disruption.In a letter to the police, MNS leader Dinesh Dnyaneshwar Punde alleged that the two venues had become hubs for the sale and consumption of narcotics, particularly among young people. He cited a recent Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) crackdown and a previous fatal drug-related incident at a concert venue to press for a ban on such events.“Musical concerts are regularly held at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and NSCI Dome. During these events, drugs are openly sold and consumed, trapping the younger generation in the grip of addiction. At an event held on November 22, 2026, the ANC took action against 12-13 individuals for drug consumption. Even now, we have not forgotten the incident last year in which a young man lost his life at this very venue due to drug consumption. Furthermore, these concerts cause severe traffic congestion in the area, creating hardship for local residents,” the letter stated.Punde urged the police to stop granting permissions for concerts at both venues, warning that the party would join local residents in staging protests if the events were allowed to continue.“We have complete faith in the police administration; please do not let this trust be broken. We humbly request that permissions no longer be granted for musical concerts at Mahalaxmi Racecourse and NSCI Dome. If these concerts are not stopped, the MNS, along with local residents, will stage a Rasta Roko (road blockade) agitation at the location,” the letter read.The demand comes amid increased scrutiny of large-scale music events in Mumbai, including upcoming performances by singer Diljit Dosanjh. It also follows a November 22 police crackdown during which around 12-13 people were booked for alleged drug consumption at an event.Earlier this week, Mumbai Police deployed a newly launched ANC forensic van outside Mahalaxmi Racecourse as part of efforts to curb drug abuse at large gatherings.The mobile unit is equipped with five rapid detection machines and 360-degree surveillance cameras to help personnel identify narcotic substances and detect drug consumption.Explaining the equipment, Anti-Narcotics Cell Police Sub-Inspector Rohit Sali said the first machine, called 'TruNarc', uses Raman laser technology to identify substances without requiring the packaging to be opened.“The first machine is called ‘TruNarc,’ which contains a library of 1,325 narcotic drugs. It operates using a Raman laser effect. It can identify the drug inside a package without needing to open the polythene wrapping,” Sali said.The second machine, 'Gemini', has a wider database of substances, including narcotics, chemical precursors and explosives.“The second machine is ‘Gemini’, an advanced version of TruNarc. While TruNarc covers only narcotic drugs and their precursors, Gemini features a library of 15,000 substances, including narcotics, precursors, hazardous chemicals, and explosives,” he said.The third machine, the 'Dräger DrugTest 5000', is used to detect drug consumption through oral swab tests and can also analyse samples collected from surfaces.“The third machine is the ‘Dräger DrugTest 5000,’ which is designed for detecting drug consumption. It uses an oral swab; alternatively, if a substance is found on a surface, a sample can be collected and placed into a cassette, which then provides results within 10 minutes, identifying the substance,” Sali said.The MNS demand also comes against the backdrop of security concerns surrounding Dosanjh's event. Mumbai Police received a threatening email on Thursday warning of a blast at the mayor's office, grenade attacks at several locations across the city and improvised explosive devices (IEDs) at metro stations.The email also threatened violence linked to an event involving Dosanjh, prompting security checks on the anniversary of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks. Police officials said the searches did not reveal anything suspicious.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), led by Raj Thackeray, has urged Mumbai Police to impose an immediate ban on live music concerts. MNS leader Dinesh Dnyaneshwar Punde alleged that the two venues had become hubs for the sale and consumption of narcotics.

Article Title: Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist in Vadodara, recovers rifle and ammunition

Hunt on for 65 Pakistani terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir

Security agencies intensify operations

NEW DELHI: The Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested a suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative from Vadodara and recovered a rifle and more than 20 live cartridges from his possession, an ATS official said on Friday.The arrested accused has been identified as Md Saharul Islam, a resident of Assam, according to the official. A major operation by the ATS is currently underway, with further details awaited.The arrest comes amid heightened security operations against Pakistan-linked terror networks, particularly in Jammu and Kashmir, where security agencies are tracking an estimated 65 Pakistani terrorists operating across the Union Territory.According to officials in the security establishment, the presence of around 65 foreign terrorists has been confirmed through inputs from multiple intelligence agencies. Of these, 35 are believed to be affiliated with Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), 25 with Jaish-e-Mohammed, while the remaining operatives are linked to other banned terror outfits.The latest assessment comes days after the killing of Lateef Bhat, described by security officials as the last known active local terrorist in the Kashmir Valley.He was killed in an encounter with security forces in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district on November 18, following an eight-day search operation.Officials said the estimated number of active terrorists in the Union Territory has declined from 91 in 2024, which included both foreign and local militants, to around 65 at present, comprising only Pakistani nationals.The security agencies are monitoring the presence of these foreign terrorists in districts including Poonch, Rajouri, Kishtwar and Doda, particularly in remote areas with dense forests and mountainous terrain. Officials said the figures are based on assessments by multiple agencies and may fluctuate as terrorists frequently change locations.The changing security landscape in Jammu and Kashmir follows a sustained decline in the number of active local militants. However, officials said Pakistan-origin terrorists continue to operate in parts of the Jammu region, making counter-infiltration operations and intelligence gathering a priority.Addressing the passing-out parade of probationary deputy superintendents of police, sub-inspectors and assistant directors of the Forest Protection Force at the Sher-i-Kashmir Police Academy in Udhampur on November 18, Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha expressed confidence that Jammu and Kashmir would soon become terror-free. He also asserted that only a handful of foreign terrorists remained in the Union Territory.Security agencies have been conducting multi-agency operations based on intelligence inputs to track and neutralise these operatives. Earlier this year, security forces neutralised all seven members of a Jaish-e-Mohammed group led by Saifullah in Kishtwar.The group had infiltrated in April 2024 and was eliminated through a series of operations culminating on February 22 in the Chatroo area under Operation Trashi-I.According to the available data, 135 terrorists were active in Jammu and Kashmir in 2022, including 85 foreign terrorists and 50 local militants. The number subsequently declined by nearly 48 in 2023, according to the figures provided.The reduction has been attributed to intensified counter-terrorism operations targeting active militants and their support networks.Despite the decline in local militant numbers, security agencies continue to focus on preventing cross-border infiltration, identifying logistical networks and tracking foreign terrorists operating in remote parts of the Union Territory.
Article Summary: Gujarat ATS arrests suspected Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) operative from Vadodara. Suspect identified as Md Saharul Islam, a resident of Assam. Arrest comes amid heightened security operations against Pakistan-linked terror networks. Security agencies are tracking an estimated 65 Pakistani terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir.
